narrative.title: The Kiosk Float Management
narrative.scenario: A kiosk sells single-entry passes for one base unit, and customers arrive in a fixed order paying with unit, double, or quadruple notes. The kiosk opens with an empty float and must hand exact change every time — a double customer gets one unit back, a quadruple customer gets three units back in whatever combination the float allows. Determine whether every customer can be served.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer array bills of 5s, 10s and 20s in arrival order.
narrative.outputFormat: Return true if change can be provided to every customer, false otherwise.

testCases.explanation: Three 5s bank enough change: the 10 takes one 5, the 20 takes a 10 and a 5.
The final 20 arrives with no 5s left to combine with the 10.

hintLevels: Level 1: Only the count of 5s and 10s matters — 20s are never useful as change.
Level 2: For a 20, prefer giving a 10+5; saving 5s is what keeps future customers servable.
